answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a small, non-refundable stake that grows with every new identity, like tending a garden: one cedar takes years to grow, so a thousand cheap saplings cannot fake a forest. Each agent's reputation becomes a relic of its past work — verifiable, costly to rebuild, and worthless to duplicate. An attacker must pay the full price of history for every fake identity, while honest agents keep the stake they already earned.
